interpretation: The scope is the input/display slice of componentlibrary's component-detail catalog (buttonview, picker/*, rating, styletext, textarea, textinput, textview, toggleview). Each family repeats one mechanism: an exported @Builder function accepts a DescriptorWrapper and either renders a host component with .attributeModifier(new XAttributeModifier($$.descriptor)) (e.g. TextBuilder) or forwards the typed descriptor to a @Component child (CameraPickerBuilder -> CameraPickerComponent). @Observed descriptor classes extend CommonAttributeModifier, whose assignAttribute maps optional descriptor fields to attribute calls only when defined (CalendarPickerAttributeModifier maps edgeAlign -> instance.edgeAlign(val?.alignType, val?.offset) and textStyle). CodeGenerator classes implement CommonCodeGenerator: generate(attributes: OriginAttribute[]) switches over attribute names against per-family entity maps (e.g. toggleType/isOn/backgroundColor from ToggleAttributeMapping), applies defaults via DEFAULT_KEY when values are missing or unrecognized, and returns a templated @Component source string; ToggleCodeGenerator branches the emitted template on ToggleType.Button vs other types and derives textColor from the parsed isOn boolean. The public boundary is the set of exported @Builder functions, descriptor/modifier/generator classes and entity map data; internal state is private. Maintenance contract: adding a component detail means adding sibling Builder/Descriptor/AttributeModifier/CodeGenerator/Mapping files wired to shared CommonAttributeModifier/CommonCodeGenerator/DescriptorWrapper in viewmodel/, keeping builder-to-descriptor casts consistent and generator defaults aligned with map data.
limitations: Shared CommonAttributeModifier/CommonCodeGenerator and DescriptorWrapper semantics outside the scope are assumed, not inspected.
Runtime build/playground rendering of generated code strings is unverified; the @Builder-to-viewmodel wiring for all eight families is inferred from the uniform pattern, not exhaustively read.

interpretation: The common module's UI state contract rests on two complementary mechanisms. (1) An MVVM base triple: BaseState is an intentionally empty marker class; BaseVM<T extends BaseState> is the abstract store holding a protected `state` assigned once from initialState in the constructor, exposing public getState():T and mandating abstract sendEvent(BaseVMEvent) — feature ViewMs subclass with a concrete state type, keep mutation behind sendEvent, and events flow one-way in. Any change to state visibility, getState's return, or sendEvent's signature breaks every subclass ViewModel's compile contract. (2) A component-level observable-state contract exemplified by WebSheet: inputs are @Prop url/urlType (plus exported WebUrlType GITCODE/HARMONYOS), reactive app-wide slices arrive via @StorageProp(StorageKey.GLOBAL_INFO / WEB_LOADING), and local render state is @State loadFailed flipped only by checkWebLoaded() (initially invoked in aboutToAppear); build() enforces a deterministic precedence — web NodeContainer with a urlType-derived negative top offset (57 vs 56), else LoadingView while isLoading, else NoNetworkView whose retry callback re-runs checkWebLoaded(). Maintenance must preserve this loading>failed precedence, the AppStorage key names, and the exported WebSheetBuilder(url,urlType) @Builder entry point that feature modules bind through. Shared constant enums (FormCardAction CALL/ROUTER, CallMethod) act as stable cross-module action keys.
limitations: BaseVMEvent.ets was not preloaded; the event taxonomy and sendEvent dispatch semantics are inferred only from BaseVM's abstract signature and import.
WebUtil.checkWebLoaded/getWebNode and the producers of AppStorage keys GLOBAL_INFO/WEB_LOADING lie outside the scope; their update/persistence behavior is unproved.

Observable behavior: serviceInit() subscribes to distributed-account login/logout common events, restores the persisted UserAccount from PreferenceManager key 'userAccount', queries HuaweiIDProvider state and resolves InitResult{isLogin,needUpdate}; login() runs a forced authorization (profile scope, serviceauthcode, PS256, random state checked against response state); logout paths clear nickname/unionId/avatarUrl, persist 'userLogin', and emit BIND_LOGOUT_EVENT. PushServiceManager requests notification enable then posts pushService.getToken() to PushService, a stub resolving true. UpdateService guards canIUse, derives UIAbilityContext from AppStorage UI_CONTEXT, and rejects BusinessError-like objects when context or capability is missing. Public boundary: singleton classes and stateless static utils exposing Promise<boolean>, InitResult, PushTokenParams; cross-boundary relations import out-of-scope storagemanager/PreferenceManager and constant/CommonConstants event ids. Maintenance contract: preserve singleton semantics, emitted events, preference keys, TAG-prefixed hilog logging (domain 0xFF00, prefix '[HMOSWorld]'), login state validation, and the index.ets barrel; PushService.postPushToken is an intentional integration seam.

interpretation: Responsibility: hmosword-build is a Node.js bootstrap helper that clones external HarmonyOS_Samples repos per config/mock.json into ../submodules/ and rewrites each so it registers as a feature module in build-profile.json5. Behavior: index.js needs fs/path/child_process + json5; readMock iterates mock.json.data; per item derives sampleName + samplePath, skips clone if non-empty, else async `git clone -b <branch> <originalUrl> <samplePath>`; processSample/processSampleWithoutConfig then rewrite the clone (entry->moduleName rename, oh-package.json5.name rewrite, src/main/module.json5 -> type='feature'/deliveryWithInstall=false/abilities[0].name=abilityName/exported=false); configured samples map clone build-profile.json5 modules entry->feature/others leaf; writeBuildProfile appends new modules to parent build-profile.json5.modules; only entry-derived entries carry default-product targets.
limitations: Whether `git clone -b <branch>` succeeds for every originalUrl/branch pair in config/mock.json is unverified: network reachability, SSH/auth availability, and rename drift in the upstream HarmonyOS_Samples repos are not provable from this checkout.

Whether the rewritten modules actually compile under hvigor is unverified; processSampleWithoutConfig only mutates modules whose existing type is 'entry', and silently skips samples whose ohosTest-only module.json5 tree yields an empty cloneSamples list.

The substringFromStartToEnd(moduleName, 6) naming convention assumes every configured moduleName is exactly 6 characters longer than the desired directory name; off-by-one or character-set edge cases are not exercised here.

deleteExtraDir is invoked with (samplePath, needModules) but its declared third parameter moduleName is never used; the cleanup semantics for samples whose build-profile.json5 is missing or whose needModules list is empty are not validated by the source alone.

interpretation: IapDataModel.ets is a 52-line, logic-free declaration module that fixes the type vocabulary of the app's IAP contract. It declares PurchaseData (the JWS envelope with optional jwsPurchaseOrder/jwsSubscriptionStatus), PurchaseOrderPayload (purchase fields incl. finishStatus), the subscription chain SubGroupStatusPayload -> SubscriptionStatus -> optional lastPurchaseOrder/renewalInfo, and string-valued enums FinishStatus ('1'/'2') and SubStatus ('1','2','3','5') mirroring IAP status codes; SubRenewalInfo stays module-private. Maintenance contract: field names, optionality, and enum values are load-bearing. Pages JSON.parse IAPKit strings (after JWSUtil.decodeJwsObj base64url decoding) and blind-cast to these interfaces with no runtime validation, so renaming a field or changing an enum value silently changes consumer branching (finishStatus !== FINISHED gates finishPurchase; status === ACTIVE gates product display) instead of failing loudly. Any edit must stay in sync with IAPKit server payload shapes and all four importing pages at once, and new IAP fields belong here rather than inline in pages.
limitations: No IAPKit server payload sample or schema exists in the repository, so the claim that the interface field names and enum string values exactly match live IAP JWS payloads is inferred from consumer usage and the sample readme, not verified against the service.

The four page consumers typecast JSON.parse results to these interfaces with 'as'; whether ArkTS type checking or any runtime guard ever rejects mismatched payload shapes was not tested, as no build, compiler run, or device execution was performed.

Fields such as SubGroupStatusPayload.environment, applicationId, packageName, and historySubscriptionStatusList appear unconsumed in the current pages; whether they are reserved for future IAP features or dead declarations is unproved.

SubscriptionsPage comments mention signature verification of jwsSubscriptionStatus, but JWSUtil.decodeJwsObj only base64url-decodes; whether cryptographic JWS verification happens elsewhere is not established by this scope.

interpretation: The componentdetailview layout-collection scope (columnview, flex, grid, list, rowview, stackview, swiperView, tabview, waterflow) implements a uniform per-component pattern: a viewmodel CodeGenerator consumes OriginAttribute[] and emits a complete ArkUI component source snippet; an AttributeMapping entity supplies map data keyed by DEFAULT_KEY for default attribute code; a Descriptor holds typed attribute state; and an @Observed AttributeModifier extends CommonAttributeModifier<Descriptor, Attribute>, overriding applyNormalAttribute to push descriptor getters onto the rendered instance via assignAttribute (e.g. Row/Column alignItems, Stack alignContent). GridCodeGenerator.generate mutates private fields by switching on attribute.name (columnsGap, rowsGap, columnsNum/rowsNum via StringUtil.getTemplateString, operationMode via JSON.parse), then returns a template literal containing the Grid's scroller, gap, template and drag/drop behavior (onItemDragStart/onItemDrop with pixelMapBuilder from grid/component/PixelMapBuilder). interpretation: This scope owns HMOS World's persistence and telemetry: two RDB stacks plus a preference store feeding a click/exposure pipeline. TrackManager (singleton) resets preference key APP_TRACK_DATA, builds TrackCommonData from AppStorage BUNDLE_INFO and deviceInfo, opens TrackTable, and registers UIObserver 'willClick' and 'navDestinationSwitch' listeners; reportData stamps time and inserts TrackServiceData, and a 60s interval queries all rows, wraps them in TrackModel, posts via TrackService.postTrackData, then deletes all rows on success or above 1000 buffered rows. TrackTable maps TrackServiceData to ValuesBucket with null-coalescing and back via sealData; RdbStore opens 'hmosWorldDatabase.db' (S1), creates the 13-column trackTable, runs insert/delete/query in @Concurrent taskpool tasks typed by TableTypeEnum, returning [] on query failure. Separately, database/FormRdbHelper (singleton over RdbUtils, 'database.db' S1) CRUDs FormInfoTable; PreferenceManager ('HMosWorldStoreWithNet') stores JSON-stringified values with one re-init retry and deletes keys whose JSON fails to parse; PreferenceCacheHelper layers Record sub-key get/set; MockRequest serves rawfile mock JSON. Cross-boundary: TrackServiceData/TrackModel/TrackEventType come from ../model/TrackModel.ets. Contract: keep store names, security levels, null-vs-absent bucket semantics and the sqlite_sequence reset stable; TrackService.postTrackData is a true-resolving stub whose real upload must preserve delete-only-on-success.
limitations: TrackService.postTrackData resolving true is assumed to be a placeholder for an unimplemented upload endpoint; no network, server, or dispatch behavior is provable from this source tree.
